prose_updates.tldr: For independently and uniformly half-randomized populations on two unequal market sides, the optimal covering rectangle at required support \(R\) reduces to a finite residual catalog depending only on \(R\). For \(R\ge4\) and \(n_B,n_S\ge4R\), the exact frontier is the maximum of finitely many affine catalog scores and every tie is retained. On balanced squares at \(R=4\), the unrestricted rectangular optimum is exactly \(2(n-1)^2+2\), strictly exceeds the published equal-block optimum for every \(n\ge3\), and has a sharp retention-ratio lower envelope \(2-4/n+4/n^2\) with limit inferior two. A constant-incidence sampler implements the selected event, and null-adjusted focal outcomes yield exact one-sided inversion for a sharp constant total effect. No universal collapse of the catalog to diagonal unit residuals is claimed.

project_justification.gap: The closest exact two-sided-market method proves validity for selected equal blocks and treats block choice within that restricted family; even on balanced square populations it does not optimize over unequal block sizes. General biclique methods establish validity and power guidance but do not classify the optimal covering paired rectangle. Marketplace bias-and-variance analyses motivate the design problem but do not solve this exact rectangle optimization, and existing one-dimensional subset-sum purification does not preserve a prescribed common buyer--seller target fiber.
project_justification.niche: Balanced independent randomization converts admissible covering rectangles into two coupled half-sum profiles. This structure permits an exact finite residual reduction and affine phase analysis for unequal market-side sizes. In the balanced \(R=4\) slice it also yields an exact infinite-family comparison with the published equal-block class, without asserting an unrestricted-biclique optimum.
project_justification.fill: A two-stage concentration argument bounds the residual on the smaller side and uses a support-preserving residual-copy comparison to bound the larger residual. This yields a finite catalog, an exact affine frontier with all catalog ties, and, at \(R=4\), the formula \(2(n-1)^2+2\) versus an equal-block upper bound \(n^2\). The resulting strict gap is at least \((n-2)^2\) and the sharp ratio lower envelope tends to two. The same catalog supports an implementable conditional law and exact one-sided sharp-null inversion. Whether every catalog entry can be purified to a dominating diagonal unit-residual entry remains a separate open question.

prose_updates.related_work: Liu, Shaikh, and Toulis (2026) establish the equal \(k\)-block total-effect test and motivate the support--focal-size trade-off; the present result optimizes over covering paired rectangles through a finite residual catalog and, on every balanced square at \(R=4\), proves exact strict superiority over their equal-block optimum with a sharp factor-two asymptotic lower envelope. Puelz, Basse, Feller, and Toulis (2022) encode imputable tests as bicliques and motivate large bicliques, but do not supply the paired-rectangle classification. Li, Zhao, Johari, and Weintraub (2021) study interference-induced bias and variance in two-sided marketplace experiments, and Johari, Li, Liskovich, and Weintraub (2022) analyze bias under two-sided platform designs; both motivate why focal retention and design choice matter, but neither is a competing exact covering-rectangle optimization result. Basse, Feller, and Toulis (2019) provide the conditioning-mechanism validity theorem used after imputability is verified. Basse, Ding, Feller, and Toulis (2024) provide the orbit-equivariance template, while unequal rectangular profiles require a separate constant-incidence count. Luo, Dasgupta, Xie, and Liu (2021) provide discrete Fisher inversion machinery, specialized here after null-adjusted dyadic imputability and crossing monotonicity are established. Singhal (2019) motivates bilinear subset-sum profiles and one-dimensional purification, but does not furnish a coupled common-fiber-preserving reduction to diagonal unit residuals. Ye et al. (2023) provide the unequal-side marketplace consumer through Platform O's independent user-view and ad randomizations.
prose_updates.interpretation: The finite-catalog result is the actionable design certificate: for fixed resolution \(R\), one enumerates \(\mathcal C_R\), evaluates the affine scores at the two market sizes, and retains every maximizer on a phase boundary. The balanced-square \(R=4\) slice gives a particularly transparent consequence: the optimal rectangular focal count is \(2(n-1)^2+2\), whereas the best published equal-block profile retains at most \(n^2\); equality in that comparator bound occurs exactly for even \(n\). Thus the rectangular-to-equal-block retention ratio is bounded below by \(2-4/n+4/n^2\), attains that bound for even \(n\), and has limit inferior two. The unresolved unit-residual question concerns only whether the already finite computation admits a further universal closed-form collapse; it is not needed for catalog optimality, the infinite strict comparison, sampling, or exact one-sided inversion.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The note proves the finite residual catalog, exact affine frontier and catalog equality cases, the infinite balanced-square \(R=4\) strict separation from the published equal-block class with sharp factor-two limit inferior, the constant-incidence sampler, and exact one-sided inversion under the sharp constant total-effect null. Universal unit-residual purification remains an explicit unresolved question and is not used by those results. The note makes no claim about weak-null validity, power or confidence-width optimality, unrestricted bicliques, minimality of the \(4R\) threshold, ordinary two-sided \(95\)-percent inversion at support \(20\), or the empirical validity of the constant-effect exposure model for Platform O.

statement_notes.justification: An infinite exact separation shows that the catalog is not merely a notational enlargement of the published equal-block family: at every balanced square with support four, unequal blocks strictly improve focal retention, with a sharp factor-two asymptotic lower envelope.
statement_notes.gap: The published equal-square calculation optimizes only over equal block sizes and therefore misses the exact unequal-block optimum even on every balanced square at support four.
statement_notes.consumer: Researchers using the published equal-block rule obtain a certified focal-size improvement for every balanced population size at least three, without changing the underlying independent balanced randomization.

statement_notes.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel: an exact all-resolution value and complete catalog equality classification over unequal margins, with the balanced support-four family giving an explicit strict comparator consequence.
statement_notes.gap: Liu, Shaikh, and Toulis optimize within a chosen equal-block family, while general biclique methods do not provide an explicit structured optimum; marketplace bias-and-variance studies motivate the problem without solving this exact combinatorial frontier.
statement_notes.consumer: A platform can choose the largest focal rectangle attaining a prespecified exact-test resolution before inspecting outcomes.
